newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi-U.S. trade up 12 pct to $16.7bln in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Saudi-U.S. trade up 12 pct to $16.7bln in 1996.

text.p: Trade between the United States and its biggest commercial partner in the Middle East, Saudi Arabia, grew 12 percent last year to $16.7 billion, U.S. commerce department counsellor Jan Kalicki said on Wednesday.
In an address to Saudi and American businessmen in Jeddah, the text of which was sent to Reuters, Kalicki said U.S. companies had invested over $6.7 billion in Saudi Arabia up until the end of 1996.
He said this represented over 46 percent of total foreign investment in the kingdom.
"The United States supplies over 20 percent of Saudi Arabia's import market and purchases about 15 percent of its exports," Kalicki said.
Total U.S. trade with the six Gulf Arab states grew 16 percent last year to almost $25 billion, equally divided between exports and imports in both directions.
Kalicki said U.S. firms had invested an estimated $9.4 billion in the Gulf states in 1995.
The GCC, an economic and political alliance, is made up of Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman, UAE and Qatar.
Kalicki said the United States and several GCC countries were close to agreement on exempting from taxation each other's income from aviation and shipping.
